entries.title: Clinical audit designs, two-phase inference, and the simulation-to-practice synthesis
entries.section: Problem, statistical model, and two-phase audit design
entries.evidence_status: SCOPE of the `catmech` package and MEASURED_DATED summary of the 10 frozen validation archives.

entries.section: Problem, statistical model, and two-phase audit design
entries.evidence_status: DEFINITION of the three conventional audit analysis choices and ANALYTIC errors-in-variables attenuation mechanism.

entries.title: Data generating and contamination framework: latent truth, corruption indicator, recorded value, and Phase II reference

entries.section: Problem, statistical model, and two-phase audit design

entries.title: Marginalized corruption probability for unaudited records via Gaussian convolution

entries.evidence_status: ANALYTIC closed-form marginal corruption probability `p_i` under Gaussian convolution.

entries.title: Conjugate Gaussian posterior for contaminated unaudited records and reference anchoring
entries.section: Problem, statistical model, and two-phase audit design
entries.evidence_status: ANALYTIC conjugate Gaussian conditional posterior for `T_i` and MCMC convergence gate.

education_contract.audience: Biostatisticians, clinical trialists, epidemiologists, and R package users analyzing audited measurements

jargon_registry.definition_literal: Audits check a small slice of records against a trusted reference.
Each row has a hidden true value and a recorded value.
The Barnard-Rubin formula caps degrees of freedom below the complete-data limit.
Linear models use a leave-one-site-out jackknife variance across clinical sites.

items.prompt: Why does discarding unaudited recorded values W_i and applying standard MAR multiple imputation (reference_normal) lose precision compared with catmech_reference(use_recorded = TRUE)?
items.answer_key: Because most unaudited recorded values W_i contain substantial valid signal about T_i; retaining W_i as a calibration predictor cuts RMSE by 43% to 48% on ClinicalTrials.gov and NHANES.

items.prompt: In catmech_contamination(), how is the latent true value T_i updated on an unaudited row when delta_i = 0 versus delta_i = 1?
items.answer_key: When delta_i = 0 (uncorrupted), T_i = W_i deterministically; when delta_i = 1 (corrupted), T_i is drawn from the precision-weighted conjugate Gaussian posterior combining X_i beta and W_i - mu_e.

items.prompt: How does catmech prevent anti-conservative confidence intervals when pooling across m imputations in studies with few clinical sites C or few survival events d?
items.answer_key: It applies the Barnard-Rubin (1999) finite-sample adjustment nu_BR with nu_com = C - 1 for clustered models (using CV3, CR1S, or Lin-Wei covariance) and nu_com = d - p for unclustered Cox PH models.

items.prompt: Why did Simple Linear MI (cole_mi) break down in the synthetic error_gross_and_small stress scenario while catmech_contamination() maintained 94.0% coverage?
items.answer_key: Gross 10x transcription outliers severely attenuated the linear calibration slope gamma_W (bias -0.2354, 64.7% coverage), whereas the contamination mixture isolated gross outliers via delta_i = 1.

items.prompt: Does a passing result (miscalibration_detected = FALSE) from catmech_holdout_check() prove that downstream regression slopes are unbiased?
items.answer_key: No; held-out row checks test observation-level prediction and had low power against regression slope bias (0/40 alarms in nonlinear_target and 1/40 in heavy_tail_target).

items.prompt: Can per-record posterior corruption probabilities p_i from catmech_contamination() be used to flag or adjudicate individual patient rows in diffuse real-world audits?
items.answer_key: No; when discrepancies are diffuse relative to T_i | X_i, per-record p_i has near-chance discrimination (AUC = 0.543 on ClinicalTrials.gov, 0.500 on NHANES, and 0.501-0.582 on Rwanda HMIS).

items.prompt: What is the validation status of catmech_audit_plan(), and why?
items.answer_key: It carries a pre-specified NO-GO validation status (exploratory only) because its median error in predicting interval width at a 5% audit fraction was 11.3% to 16.8%, exceeding the 10% tolerance.

items.prompt: Does generating a report with catmech_audit_trail() certify that an analysis is compliant with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E9?
items.answer_key: No; SHA-256 provenance records support reproducibility and regulatory documentation, but compliance depends on the surrounding validated system, access controls, and standard operating procedures.

items.prompt: A multicenter trial has C = 12 sites and audits a continuous biomarker T_i on 25% of patients to estimate a linear regression Y ~ T + age + sex. Should the analyst fit catmech_reference(cluster = 'site')?
items.answer_key: No; because the audited variable T_i is a predictor rather than the outcome, clustered random-intercept MI attenuates the slope (up to -16.1%). Fit catmech_reference(use_recorded = TRUE) without cluster and pool with catmech_pool_lm(cluster = 'site').

items.prompt: In a biomarker audit where the true physiological distribution T_i is known to have heavy Student-t_4 tails and discrepancies are moderate, which catmech engine should be chosen?
items.answer_key: Choose catmech_reference(use_recorded = TRUE) (Simple Linear MI, 92.0% coverage in heavy_tail_target) rather than catmech_contamination(), which misclassifies genuine tail extremes as recording errors (87.3% coverage).

items.prompt: When auditing a noisy reference assay where gold-standard measurements R_i have known analytical standard deviation sigma_ref = 0.35, what happens if reference_sd is left at 0 versus set to 0.35?
items.answer_key: Leaving reference_sd = 0 triggers a universal-disagreement warning and undercoverage (88.7% in noisy_undeclared); setting reference_sd = 0.35 (noisy_declared) restores bias (-0.0071) and coverage (91.8%).

items.prompt: An unclustered oncology survival study has N = 800 patients, d = 30 observed deaths, and p = 4 covariates in catmech_pool_coxph(). What is the upper bound on the Barnard-Rubin degrees of freedom nu_BR?
items.answer_key: Because unclustered Cox PH pooling defines complete-data degrees of freedom strictly from observed failure events as nu_com = d - p = 30 - 4 = 26, nu_BR is strictly less than 26.

one_sentence_rubric.criterion: States that catmech uses two-phase audited reference measurements to calibrate contaminated or incomplete recorded values and pool downstream regressions
Distinguishes analytical posteriors/variance formulas from synthetic simulations (52,950 requests) and empirical benchmarks (CT.gov, NHANES, Rwanda HMIS)
Preserves the non-claims that per-row p_i is near chance on diffuse real data, catmech_audit_plan() is NO-GO, and catmech_audit_trail() does not certify Part 11 compliance
Selects Simple Linear MI vs Contamination Mixture and appropriate cluster pooling (CV3/CR1S/Lin-Wei) for a new clinical audit scenario
